rules-live-in-the-harness.reading: Everything built here is for the harness, used on itself: every rule he gives is cemented in the harness, in its documents and in the files that make it act, here and in every project that installs it, because what stays in memory is forgotten. Each proposal is judged both as this project's development and as the harness in production in other projects; a gap is solved by building it, ourselves or on another solution; problems seen in any session are measured and analysed as findings to improve the harness. Since the models are Anthropic's and Codex is only an outside reviewer of what is done and of a project's code, Claude works from a root CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md, and AGENTS.md keeps what a reviewer needs (diet D3, F8's S3): a rule's prose home is a line of either file, no longer AGENTS.md alone. The guard's refusal of a feedback note without a home (rule:memory-feedback-home) is its sensor. An output he sees again and again is cemented the same way, so a model's taste cannot reach him: a template of five parts (the sample he approved, the command that renders it from the records, a golden test, a gate on the path to him, and a test that the gate refuses a hand-made one), asked for in one line, "Plantilla: qué quiero ver · cuándo aparece · cómo se ve (la muestra que apruebo) · dónde me llega", a missing field asked alone, and every escape a FAILURES sighting and a new refusal test (odd/tasks/templates.md). A manual workaround is cemented too (his words of 2026-11-14, the orchestrator's transcript 69918425, lines 10967 and 11014): a step the lead or a session does by hand to get past a gap gets a follow-up that builds it into bin/, a template or a check, and a session or a roadmap entry owns it, named in the same reply that tells of the workaround, so it does not stay in memory and get lost (odd/tasks/cement-workarounds.md).
